# OuroMcpApp

The view an MCP server returns for agent-composed UI (MCP Apps): the host, such as Claude or ChatGPT, frames it, and it shows the latest tool result's `structuredContent.a2ui` with `A2UISurface`. Read and write buttons call their action's own tool through the host, a consequential one only after the person confirms, and a person-only one takes the person to your app's screen. It follows the host's light or dark theme and tells the host its size.

```tsx
import { OuroMcpApp } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/mcp-app/ouro-mcp-app";
```

## Example

```tsx
createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <OuroMcpApp catalog={catalog} handoffUrl={({ action }) => `https://kitchen.example.com/recipes?do=${action}`} />,
);
```

## Usage

Build it into one HTML file with your catalog embedded (`node scripts/mcp-app.mts build`), and serve that as the `ui://` resource.

## Use instead when

- Use A2UISurface instead when the card is in your own app's screen, not in an MCP host.

## Props

Type: `OuroMcpAppProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appInfo` | `{ name: string; version: string }` | { name: "Ouro HX card", version: "1.0.0" } | What the view calls itself in `ui/initialize`. |
| `catalog` (required) | `unknown` |  | The app's A2UI catalog, generated from its actions by core's `ouro-a2ui-catalog.mts catalog`. Tool results carry only its id. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width (`max-w-md`). |
| `handoffUrl` | `((handoff: A2UIHandoff) => string \| undefined)` |  | Where a person-only button takes the person: the address of your app's own screen for that action, which the host opens with `ui/open-link`. Without one, or when the host can't open links, the view tells the person where to do it. |
| `host` | `McpAppHostLink` | the window that framed the view, through `windowHostLink()` | The connection to the host. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `onAction`: Not a prop. A pressed button calls that action's own MCP tool through the host: give the view only the catalog.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `A2UIHandoff`

Where a person-only button takes the person: the action's id and the declaration's `how`.

```ts
interface A2UIHandoff {
  action: string;
  how: string;
}
```

### `McpAppHostLink`

How a view reaches its host: post a message to it, and hear the host's. `listen` returns the function that stops.

```ts
interface McpAppHostLink {
  post: (message: McpAppMessage) => void;
  listen: (onMessage: (message: unknown) => void) => () => void;
}
```

### `McpAppMessage`

A JSON-RPC message: a request (`id` and `method`), a notification (`method` only) or a response (`id`).

```ts
interface McpAppMessage {
  jsonrpc: "2.0";
  id?: string | number;
  method?: string;
  params?: object;
  result?: object;
  error?: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown };
}
```
